corpus_evidence.note: Adj+Adj / mood-first openings dominate the live catalog (~69% adj_pair). Visual-lead openings are rare. Repeated simple shapes are the working house style, not a defect.

discarded_from_v2: syntax variety for its own sake
avoidance of repeated openings as primary concern
Dynamic Movement / oscillation as preferred pattern
editorial richness / emotionally layered experience as goals
pressure to make every line structurally unique
long critic-elegant good examples (weave, mid-contradiction, ache, unsettles)
anti-example stack centered on Adj+Adj openings

sections.purpose: Help a user understand the film’s emotional feel at a glance. Write like a thoughtful friend — clear and immediate — not like a film critic crafting a beautiful sentence.
core_principles: First-words test: can someone understand the basic mood from the first few words?
Name the mood clearly first, then add 1–2 specifics that make it more useful for this film.
Default shape: [Mood], with [1–2 specifics]. This is a default, not a hard template.
Simple repeated sentence shapes are normal. Adj openings are normal. Structural uniformity is not a problem.
Specificity comes from the film (pace, setting, visuals, sound, technique, tonal contrast) — not from complex syntax or literary wording.
Prefer natural, simple English that is easy on first read.
Imagery or metaphor only when it is the clearest natural phrasing — never as a stylistic default.
Do not retell the synopsis or explain the film’s themes.

mood_dimensions.name: Core mood
mood_dimensions.detail: The main emotional feel, named early (tense, dreamy, bleak, playful, etc.).

mood_dimensions.name: Useful specifics
mood_dimensions.detail: Optional 1–2 cues: pace, setting, visual style, sound, technique, or a distinctive tonal contrast.

strong_patterns.why: Matches the glance test and the live catalog’s dominant house style.
Keeps the line useful without stacking style.
Easy to read aloud; no critic performance.

weak_patterns.pattern: Visual/technique lead that delays the mood
weak_patterns.when_weak: When the first words describe colors, lines, or animation before the emotional feel is clear.
weak_patterns.when_ok: Rarely; only if that visual cue is itself the fastest way to name the feel.

weak_patterns.when_weak: When the sentence sounds written to impress — stacked metaphors, elegant verbs, review-copy cadence.

weak_patterns.pattern: Empty generic mood with no film cue
weak_patterns.when_weak: When the line could fit many unrelated films (quiet and emotional, tense atmosphere, etc.).
weak_patterns.when_ok: Never — always keep at least one useful film-specific cue when available.

weak_patterns.when_weak: When the line retells plot or explains what the film is saying.

syntax_library.principle: Start with the mood (often Adj+Adj or a short mood phrase), then with 1–2 specifics. Example shape: 'Quiet and heavy, with a slow pace and stark silence.' Repeated use of this shape across films is fine.

sections.specificity_test: Do the first few words name the mood? Is the rest easy on first read? Is there at least one concrete cue that belongs to this film?
sections.relationship_with_synopsis: Complement the synopsis. Describe watching-feel; do not retell plot.
sections.relationship_with_moods_tags: Do not list tags. Turn the main feelings into plain mood-first language.

good_examples.title: A Silent Voice
good_examples.the_mood: Quiet and heavy, with a slow pace that amplifies discomfort and isolation, contrasting moments of warmth with stark silence.
good_examples.why: Mood first; catalog house style; concrete pace/silence cues.

good_examples.title: 5 Centimeters per Second
good_examples.the_mood: Slow and melancholic, with a stark contrast between vibrant visuals and emotional distance.

good_examples.title: Approved for Adoption
good_examples.the_mood: Warm and textured, with a mix of humor and melancholy, balancing light animation with moments of stark realism.

good_examples.title: Another Day of Life
good_examples.the_mood: Urgent and chaotic, blending stark realism with stylized animation, punctuated by dark humor and tension.
good_examples.why: Mood first; specifics earn their place.

good_examples.title: Seoul Station
good_examples.the_mood: Relentless and claustrophobic, with gritty 2D textures and urgent pacing that heighten urban dread.
good_examples.why: Glance-readable; discovery batch already worked this way.

good_examples.title: Boys Go to Jupiter (mood-first model)
good_examples.the_mood: Dreamy and slow, with soft pastel Florida suburbia and sudden surreal daydream flashes.
good_examples.why: Default shape; film-owned cues without literary stacking.

good_examples.title: Padak (mood-first model)
good_examples.the_mood: Claustrophobic and bleak, with cold blues and tight framing trapping a mackerel in slow dread.
good_examples.why: Mood first while keeping the film’s concrete image.

good_examples.title: Fritz the Cat (mood-first model)
good_examples.the_mood: Restless and unhinged, with gritty 2D chaos and loud irreverent humor in late-60s New York nights.

anti_examples.title: Visual-lead delay
anti_examples.the_mood: Shadowy stop-motion puppets move with slow, deliberate rhythms, weaving eerie textures and a haunting, wordless tension in a dark forest.
anti_examples.why: Technique/visuals first; literary density; mood arrives late.

anti_examples.title: Critic stacking
anti_examples.the_mood: Rain-soaked Naples hums with muted colors and layered city sounds as quiet grief and fleeting connections unfold in slow, intimate rhythms.
anti_examples.why: Sounds written to impress; hard to glance.

anti_examples.title: Empty generic
anti_examples.the_mood: Quiet and emotional, with an intimate and reflective atmosphere.

anti_examples.title: Theme analysis
anti_examples.the_mood: Gritty 2D animation pulses with chaotic energy, reflecting late-60s counterculture and social upheaval.

final_guide.analyst_notes: Minimal reset guide. Built from the live catalog’s dominant mood-first / Adj+Adj house style and the product glance test. Deliberately omits v2 goals around syntax variety, anti-repetition, oscillation, and sensory cascade.
